title: Interruptible self-heal
subtitle: Make recovery a readable, bounded action with a real stop window
summary: The boss starts a visible recovery action without player contact; a qualified interruption cancels it, while a completed cast applies one capped heal.
overview: An interruptible self-heal asks whether the player can trade position or damage for preserving progress. The heal begins from a boss action, exposes a deadline, and resolves once only after completion. The signal, interruption rule, amount, cooldown, and post-cast opening must remain readable.
learning: Define the start condition, channel duration, qualifying interrupt, super-armor policy, completion frame, requested and applied healing, overheal, de-duplication, cooldown, phase carryover, rollback, and telemetry that links one cast id to one result.

demo.title: Interrupt Kern’s first channel with Tavi’s sword, then let the second channel finish
demo.step: Signal, cancel, recast, and healing states
phaseDescriptions: At 0.30 s, Kern opens a runic ring and commits to a 0.68-second channel. The inward motes and filling cast bar expose the deadline before any health changes.
Tavi reaches Kern and lands a sword strike at 1.46 s. The ring breaks, the first cast records one interruption, and Kern remains at 38 health.
Kern begins a second channel at 3.02 s. With no qualified hit before 4.18 s, the cast completes once and restores 24 health, raising Kern from 38 to 62 before recovery.
demo.danger: Only a completed cast may heal; an interrupted attempt applies zero, and repeated callbacks for the same cast id cannot create extra healing
demo.locked: Start condition, channel deadline, interrupt tags, armor, requested and applied healing, cap, cooldown, cast id, phase transition, rollback, and persistence belong to encounter logic
demo.safe: Show a distinct pose, inward motion, cast progress, interruption break, boss-health change, and a recovery window after either outcome
demo.reducedMotion: Autoplay is disabled by reduced motion. Scrub across 0.30, 0.78, 1.28, 1.46, 2.54, 3.02, 4.18, 4.40, 4.62, and 5.36 seconds to inspect both attempts and the reset.
demo.diagramDescription: Kern channels inside concentric runic circles while motes travel inward and a cast bar fills. Tavi breaks the first ring with a sword slash; the second ring completes and the boss health bar rises once from 38 to 62.

steps.title: What starts the heal and how often may it occur?
steps.body: Choose health, phase, timer, or tactical conditions explicitly. Gate the action with a cooldown or limited charges so the boss cannot immediately recast until the encounter becomes a progress reset.

steps.title: What qualifies as an interruption?
steps.body: Define damage threshold, stagger tag, status, tool, hit direction, and super-armor. Resolve the answer on the authoritative combat event, cancel the pending heal, and record one stable cast id with its rejection reason.

steps.title: What happens on completion or cancellation?
steps.body: Apply healing once on the completion frame, clamp it at maximum health, then enter a clear recovery. A cancelled cast should heal zero and still give readable confirmation and a deliberately tuned punish window.

mistakes.title: Health rises before the channel visibly completes
mistakes.body: If the bar moves during wind-up, the player cannot know whether an interruption worked. Keep pending and applied healing separate, and commit the health change on one explicit completion event.

mistakes.title: The boss recasts until progress is erased
mistakes.body: An unbounded trigger turns healing into repetition instead of a decision. Limit frequency and amount, preserve a response window, and compare restored health with expected player damage per opening.

designNotes.title: Model the cast as a transaction
designNotes.body: Store castId, startedAt, completesAt, interruptedAt, healRequested, healApplied, and result. This prevents duplicated completion callbacks and makes rollback and save-state restoration deterministic.

designNotes.title: Price the interrupt route
designNotes.body: Measure travel time, required damage, consumed resources, and exposure to other attacks. The player should decide whether preserving progress is worth leaving safety or spending a scarce answer.

designNotes.title: Instrument both outcomes
designNotes.body: Track cast starts, interruption rate and timing, completed heals, overheal, health restored per minute, recast intervals, damage traded for interrupts, deaths after completion, and phase duration.

story.title: Tavi splits Kern’s gathering rune
story.body: Light begins to crawl from the arena stones toward the cracks in Kern’s chest. Tavi crosses the circle and cuts through its central glyph; the fragments dim before they can seal the elemental.

adaptation.title: Expose the deadline through more than color
adaptation.body: Combine pose, sound cadence, inward particles, cast progress, and a completion pulse. Offer a longer window, lower interrupt threshold, reduced heal, fewer casts, or a dedicated counter prompt without changing the underlying rule.

distinction.title: Scheduled recovery, not healing from contact
distinction.body: Self-healing begins from a boss decision or encounter condition and can expose a channel. On-hit healing requires eligible contact with a target, while an external healing source belongs to another entity that may be attacked separately.

lensNotes.body: The cast bar, boss health, and result id show exactly when pending recovery becomes applied recovery.
A reachable deadline and explicit interrupt predicate let the player prevent the heal instead of merely enduring it.
Interrupting may require leaving safety or spending damage and resources, while accepting the heal preserves position.
Super-armor, status immunity, phase changes, duplicate hits, overheal, and rollback need explicit outcomes.
The healing intent must be distinguishable from an attack before the player commits to approaching.

examples.body: At 2:17, Vicar Amelia withdraws and begins her prayer while the hunter selects Numbing Mist. The long pose and golden recovery state create a response window; damage can interrupt it, while the item temporarily blocks further healing.

At 0:17, the Collector drinks the Panacea behind a protective field and restores health. Early protected drinks teach the rule safely; the final unshielded drink changes the same readable action into an interruption objective.

At 1:53, Sabrina’s Alakazam uses Recover in a turn-based exchange. The move has no spatial channel, so the command text and HP bar carry the entire signal and result contract; the encounter still needs limits that prevent endless progress reversal.
